evidence.excerpt: This study investigated the effect of modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) on the postharvest quality and shelf life of Serbian-grown raspberries intended for export markets. Three gas compositions — 5% O₂/15% CO₂/80% N₂, 10% O₂/10% CO₂/80% N₂, and ambient air control — were evaluated at 2 °C storage over a 14-day period. Quality parameters including firmness, color (L*, a*, b*), soluble solids content, titratable acidity, and visual mold incidence were monitored at two-day intervals. Microbiological analyses targeted total aerobic counts and Botrytis cinerea colony formation. Results demonstrated that the 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere reduced Botrytis incidence by 63% relative to control and maintained firmness above commercial acceptability thresholds for 12 days compared to 6 days in ambient conditions. Sensory panel scores for color and texture confirmed marketability at day 10 under optimal MAP conditions. The findings provide actionable gas-mix specifications for exporters shipping raspberries to Central European markets, and establish a data foundation for integrating MAP parameters into predictive shelf-life models. Practical recommendations for film permeability selection and pallet-level gas management are discussed.
